agent.problem: The transition explicitly uses the rulers from verse 1 as well as the move to how believers speak in verse 2, but the card cites only Titus 3:2. Its citation is too narrow and should begin at Titus 3:1.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

agent.problem: The right answer, everyone, includes both believers and leaders. A baker could therefore argue that Paul wants full consideration shown to either of those groups too, so the wrong answers are not cleanly distinguishable from the right answer.

rule.text: A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

agent.problem: No card includes the last sentence of Titus 3:8, that these things are excellent and profitable for the people. That leaves out an important part of Paul's movement from devotion to good deeds in verse 8 to the pointless and worthless things in verse 9.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

human.problem: Stop 1 ends at Titus 3:5, in the middle of one sentence that runs from 3:4 to 3:7. Stop 2 then picks up with "This is the Spirit He poured out" (3:6). The reveal screen after stop 1 will show a sentence cut off partway. Moving the break to 3:7 or 3:8 would keep the thought whole and still fit the card limits (stop 1 would have about 19 cards).
human.question: Should a stop be allowed to end in the middle of a sentence or a single thought in the passage, or should stop breaks fall at natural sentence or thought boundaries?
